LaunchDarkly Release Autopilot helps remove that risk, giving teams the power to automatically configure, execute, monitor, and complete releases without engineers manually setting up flags, coordinating rollouts, or cleaning up afterward. tech.title: Anthropic IPO raises over $81 billion in largest offering on record, topping SpaceX
tech.summary: Anthropic sold about 980 million shares priced at $83 per share at its IPO on Wednesday. The AI lab raised $81.3 billion and now has a fully diluted market cap of around $1.5 trillion. The stock is expected to begin trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker symbol 'ANT'. OpenAI's IPO will likely debut in 2027.

tech.title: A Tesla Model Y Without A Steering Wheel Is Coming
tech.summary: Tesla plans to create a fully autonomous vehicle that can seat more than two people. It is developing an autonomous version of the Model Y without a steering wheel or pedals. The vehicle will be designed for transporting groups of people and will be able to seat up to six or seven passengers. Tesla will continue to manufacture regular Model Ys with steering wheels for the foreseeable future.

tech.title: Hardware Is Software
tech.summary: Most hardware engineering is actually software engineering in disguise. Everything is a calculation, and calculation is software. The industry is currently doing these calculations essentially by hand, as if it were doing arithmetic without having yet discovered algebra. Hardware engineers need to design algorithms for designing their hardware. This allows small teams to build big things.

tech.title: Unblockable communication with gravity
tech.summary: All modern wireless communication technologies are based on electromagnetism, which is readily susceptible to screening and blocking. Gravity is a viable platform for practically unblockable communication. This study proposes and implements a wireless communication protocol where a broadcaster encodes a binary message by moving a mass, and a receiver detects the resulting gravitational signal with an off-the-shelf, hand-held gravimeter.

tech.title: AWS announces ExtendDB 1.0
tech.summary: ExtendDB is a production-ready Amazon DynamoDB-compatible adapter. It is fully compatible with the DynamoDB API and can run on PostgreSQL, SQLite, Cassandra, and MongoDB. ExtendDB allows developers and infrastructure teams to run DynamoDB workloads in on-premise data centers, in private or public clouds, and at the edge, without rewriting application code. It is open source under the Apache 2.0 license.

tech.title: Foundation Software
tech.summary: Open source projects are being flooded with PRs thanks to AI. Instead of submitting these PRs, developers should publish forks with no expectation of merging. Maintainers could then search through the forks and see what other people are building, then choose which changes to make upstream. This search could be done with agents hunting for patterns.

tech.title: Nvidia interim CEO Kress tells employees ‘let's move forward' at first all-hands meeting since Jensen Huang exit
tech.summary: Nvidia recently held its first all-hands meeting since its founder, Jensen Huang, resigned. The meeting opened with a message about moving forward. Executives announced that pay rises and the yearly review process will be moved up from March to December. There appears to be division in the company about whether to reinstate Huang, but the company's newly appointed board chair has said that the board does not intend to do so.

tech.title: On Waymos and their safety record
tech.summary: Waymo has little incentive to prioritize road safety beyond a self-determined limit. Once the company captures a significant market share, a board will decide what an acceptable level of road fatalities is. The company can eat any amount of fine payments. Waymo cannot solve road safety - it can only shift the locus of policy around road safety away from the government into an unaccountable corporation.

tech.title: Text2SQL agents waste tokens. Neo4j cuts usage by up to 81%
tech.summary: Text2SQL agents get expensive when they scan a large schema for every question. With compact graph-based retrieval, token usage drops and accuracy improves. Build your knowledge graph on Neo4j

webdev.title: Understanding CSS random()
webdev.summary: CSS random() can give elements distinct values that stay consistent across breakpoints and animations. This worked example explains how cache keys, property positions, and explicit scopes determine whether random values are shared, regenerated, or fixed for debugging.

webdev.title: Sashiko: Lessons from Building an Agentic Code Review System for Linux
webdev.summary: Sashiko separates specialist bug discovery from verification, requiring code evidence for both findings and dismissals. Its review pipeline gathers surrounding context, investigates uncertain cases individually, and publishes its reasoning, with production data showing a correlation between clean reviews and fewer follow-up fixes.

webdev.title: The Magic of Partial Evaluation
webdev.summary: Partial evaluation executes the parts of a program whose inputs are already known and leaves specialized code for the remaining work. This post has examples that build from arithmetic and schema validation to the Futamura projections, showing how specializing an interpreter can produce compiled programs and even a compiler.

webdev.title: We Stopped a Railway Migration Three Weeks Out
webdev.summary: A production migration was canceled after database import times and operational constraints made the cutover too difficult to predict. The retrospective argues for pricing recovery, observability, storage limits, and maintenance work alongside compute, while noting that its import runs were not a controlled within-tier benchmark.

webdev.title: The Codebase Is the Harness
webdev.summary: Agent tooling, instructions, review processes, and product code can evolve together inside one repository. One workflow uses session recordings to diagnose user-facing bugs and then updates instructions after fixes, with a person still setting the broader direction.

webdev.title: Traffic Mix Matters
webdev.summary: A load test can miss production failures when it reproduces request volume without reproducing workload distribution. Interactive simulations show key concentration reducing throughput in a lock-based system but improving it in a cached system, so the same skew can move performance in opposite directions.

Teams configure the stages, skills, and approvals, with options to use Mastra's platform, run the server locally, or self-host the supporting infrastructure.

webdev.title: Search Browser
webdev.summary: Search is a free, open-source Mac browser built on the WebKit engine already supplied by macOS. It combines spaces, pinned tabs, reading mode, and built-in blocking. The Chrome Web Store extension requires macOS 15.4 or later.

Google prices it at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens, with rollout through the Gemini API, enterprise products, Antigravity, and paid Gemini app plans.

webdev.title: Advancing Chip Design with OpenAI Models
webdev.summary: OpenAI reports model-written RTL improvements across its Jalapeño chip and AMD designs, including up to 14% improvement in power, performance, and area relative to heavily optimized GPU baselines. Separate RISC-V evaluations found stronger results when models were designed from specifications, though omitted features and simplified timing checks limit how directly those scores transfer to production.

webdev.title: LLM-Assisted Reverse Engineering
webdev.summary: This reverse-engineering workflow combines agents with Ghidra, command-line disassemblers, runtime debugging, and persistent notes. When static analysis stalls, it shifts to one recorded hypothesis at a time, using probes or logs to prove or disprove explanations instead of letting the agent keep guessing.

webdev.title: Why Is Gemini 4 Carbon Taking So Long?
webdev.summary: Traces from a private bug-fixing evaluation attribute Carbon's long runtimes to slower inference, unnecessary investigation, and repeated file reads. About half its steps addressed work outside the tickets, while periodic check-ins shortened one trial from 37 to 28 minutes, suggesting that stopping behavior contributes to the gap.

webdev.summary: Chat instead of configure with Switch Buddy. Free and self-hosted, turn your AI agents into teammates that work in GitHub, Jira, Datadog & more. Get started .

webdev.summary: An Agent Duel model projects Neon near Opus 5.5 by combining Carbon-level quality with faster generation, but the estimate is a speed-based projection with a wide uncertainty interval rather than a measured Neon leaderboard result.

webdev.title: How to Give Millions of Workflows Quality Sleep
webdev.summary: DBOS suspends waiting workflows into database records instead of retaining threads or memory, then uses indexed deadlines and notifications to resume them from checkpoints.

webdev.title: Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution in NGINX
webdev.summary: Two critical HTTP/2 memory-safety flaws can allow unauthenticated code execution in affected NGINX deployments.

webdev.summary: Polypane 32 adds MCP and CLI automation for multi-viewport testing and accessibility checks, plus a panel for inspecting and validating WebMCP tools.

webdev.title: Cloudflare CLI 1.0 Release Candidate
webdev.summary: The cf release candidate stabilizes its configuration and build formats while adding features such as live JSON log streams, deployment previews, and temporary accounts that can be claimed later.

data.title: Agentic data engineering is here! Project Osmos: What, Why, and How?
data.summary: Microsoft Fabric's Project Osmos is an AI agent that plans, builds, runs, and validates Spark data pipelines from a written specification. In a test using Vienna's public transit timetables, it built a working pipeline, but independent checks caught a daylight saving bug that the agent's own tests missed.

data.title: Rebuilding Data Lineage at LinkedIn: From Storage to Compute
data.summary: LinkedIn rebuilt its data lineage platform to capture dependencies directly from running jobs, giving engineers a more precise view of where data comes from and what depends on it. The resulting graph covers about 6 million datasets and helps teams trace incidents, assess the impact of changes, and safely retire unused pipelines.

data.title: De-identifying text at scale: How Airbnb protects personal data in AI training
data.summary: Training teams need realistic text data without letting PII leak into shared ML workflows. Airbnb packaged open-source Presidio, originally developed by Microsoft, as an in-process pipeline step, added domain-specific recognizers and multilingual evaluation, and then tagged de-identified datasets through its model registry. The useful pattern is turning privacy policy into testable, reusable data controls rather than asking every team to improvise.

data.title: MySQL tables in four open source Iceberg catalogs, read by Trino and DuckDB
data.summary: Can MySQL changes land in Iceberg without a bespoke warehouse pipeline? DBTrail followed the binlog, exported initial and incremental snapshots into four open-source REST catalogs, then checked row counts and aggregates through Trino and DuckDB against MySQL. The tests surfaced real interoperability gaps around credential vending and equality deletes—not just a happy-path compatibility claim.

data.title: Are we Finally Entering the Golden Age of Data Science?
data.summary: AI and modern data tools are making it faster to build pipelines and answer routine business questions. This gives data scientists more time to ask questions that matter, design experiments, and use AI agents to test what actually drives business outcomes.

data.title: Data Contracts
data.summary: Data contracts apply API design to datasets, describing their contents and guarantees so that people and AI agents can work with data on their own. A quality rule, such as less than 1% empty names, becomes an assertion that tooling can pass or fail. Published test results can then show how often each promise was kept.

data.title: pgvectorfast
data.summary: pgvectorfast is a drop-in replacement for pgvector that uses a faster buffer pool to speed up vector search and analytical queries in PostgreSQL.

data.title: Open Source DocumentDB 1.0 Reaches General Availability
data.summary: DocumentDB 1.0 brings an MIT-licensed, MongoDB-compatible document store to PostgreSQL through an extension and protocol gateway, letting existing drivers and queries work with a familiar relational foundation. The GA release covers PostgreSQL 15-18, adds a Kubernetes operator, and focuses on stability across indexing, aggregation, and geospatial queries.

data.title: MongoDB Acquires Firebolt
data.summary: MongoDB has acquired Firebolt and will run its analytics engine alongside the database, kept in sync automatically so there is no pipeline to build. MongoDB pitches it as removing the data-movement tax, since agents can drive thousands of concurrent queries and need sub-second answers on fresh data. It will join search, vector search, and Voyage AI models in the platform.

data.title: How one SurrealQL query scans 10 billion rows a second
data.summary: SurrealDB says its Earth database scanned more than 10 billion rows per second in a launch benchmark by splitting one query across about 1,000 Cloudflare Workers. Each worker reads a different slice of the same database snapshot, and SurrealDB checks and combines the results into one answer.

data.title: Airflow plays GTA2
data.summary: This Apache Airflow 3.4 demo uses a local AI model to drive a car through a custom delivery mission in Grand Theft Auto 2. Each move is one iteration of an Airflow task loop, and a dashcam plugin lets you watch the run live or replay it later.

data.title: Securing Enterprise Data Agents with Policy as Code: A Preflight Gate for Multi-Domain NL2SQL
data.summary: Shared service accounts can bypass the user-level controls a data agent is meant to enforce. This prototype parses generated SQL into an AST, resolves every table and column dependency, evaluates CEL policies, then prepares approved row filters before execution. Database roles remain the final guardrail. The takeaway: authorize the query's actual dependencies, not just its visible output.

data.title: Reduce Your Data Pipelines, One Database, Every Data Type
data.summary: Oracle AI Database combines relational, JSON, graph, and vector data in one engine, reducing the need to copy data into separate systems. Try it free on Oracle LiveLabs.

data.title: Data work is coding now
data.summary: AI is making it easier for anyone to analyze data and build apps by generating the code for them.

data.title: Rethinking Table File Paths with Uber: Lance's Multi-Base Layout
data.summary: Lance's multi-base layout lets one dataset span multiple storage locations, improving portability and avoiding rewrite-heavy path migrations as data scales across buckets.

marketing.title: Atlassian's AI Marketing Playbook for Campaigns, Creative Production & Reporting
marketing.summary: AI can draft a brief and content in minutes. But campaigns still take weeks to launch, creative gets trapped in revision cycles, and reporting takes hours to pull together. Atlassian's AI Marketing Playbook is a practical guide to making AI deliver for marketing, where you'll learn how to: Build stronger campaign plans, move into execution faster, and maintain momentum as priorities change. Increase creative capacity while protecting time for ideas, craft, and quality. Move from performance signals to decisions and action sooner. You'll also get a practical framework for choosing a high-value workflow to transform, piloting it on real work, and measuring the impact. Get the playbook.

marketing.title: Marketers to Spend $116 Billion on Creators in 2026
marketing.summary: Brand spending on creators is forecast to grow 15% in 2026 and reach $178 billion by 2030, about twice the pace of advertising. Paid amplification of creator content makes up 44% of spending, while paying creators for content rather than reach is the fastest-growing segment. Most of the growth comes from budgets shifted out of TV, performance media, and creative production rather than new marketing dollars.

marketing.title: 94% of global hits went viral on TikTok first, reveals 2026 Music Impact Report
marketing.summary: TikTok has become a major driver of music discovery and commercial success. 94% of songs that entered the Billboard Global 200 in 2025 went viral on the platform first. Songs that go viral on TikTok spend four times longer on the chart than non-viral tracks, and 45% of US TikTok users discover new music on the platform. That discovery also translates into purchases: TikTok music listeners are 78% more likely to pay for a streaming subscription, and 61% purchased physical or digital music in the past year.

marketing.title: Win Report: How cutting overwhelm grew conversions by 13%
marketing.summary: Reducing the effort required to compare options can increase conversions, especially when a page overwhelms visitors with too much information. Churnet Valley Railway replaced its long list of eight dining experiences with categorized sections that put popular options first and compact cards that made prices, departure times, and durations easy to compare. It also replaced the “Book Now” CTA with “Check Running Times” to give visitors a lower-commitment next step into the booking process. The redesign increased conversions by 13%, with an even stronger result among first-time visitors.

marketing.title: 5 ways to personalize your emails, from a study of 274 billion sends
marketing.summary: Personalize emails by referencing shoppers' recent activity, such as products they browsed, items in their cart, or their last purchase. Use signup preferences to tailor welcome emails, and include product-specific care tips, how-to content, or complementary product recommendations in post-purchase emails. Show/hide logic can also display different content to different segments in a single campaign, such as VIP offers for loyalty members or location-specific promotions. Klaviyo's analysis of 274 billion emails found that messages that referenced shoppers' recent activity earned 45% higher click rates in flows and 33% higher click rates in campaigns.

marketing.title: 5 tips to increasing LinkedIn video reach
marketing.summary: With LinkedIn reach declining, prioritize timely topics tied to current conversations and use on-screen text hooks that create curiosity rather than simply describe the video. Keep footage clear and audio crisp without overcomplicating production. Focus on content that offers value viewers can apply or save. Listicles and self-improvement formats are gaining traction. Avoid excessive transitions and visual effects that distract from the message.

marketing.title: What's Next for AI Search in 2027 with Kevin Indig and Eli Schwartz
marketing.summary: Should you be writing 10x more blog posts? Chasing citations on Reddit? Or a different strategy altogether? On December 8 , AI search exports Kevin Indig and Eli Schwartz will dive into the data, the myths - and three bets on where to invest next. Register now

marketing.title: The AI Ad Creative Masterclass: Skills, Tools, and the 21 Formats Top Brands Run
marketing.summary: 24 of the 34 longest-running Meta ads from 48 top DTC brands were simple stills. Creator videos were the most tested video format but among the first switched off, with a median run of 38 days. Strong batches mix at least 4 formats and 3 buying angles, with stills built to run for months and videos replaced every few weeks.

marketing.title: WriteStack
marketing.summary: WriteStack is a Substack growth platform that helps creators turn Notes into free and paid subscribers. Its AI Coach generates Notes and outlines in the creator's voice and helps edit articles. Creators can batch schedule Notes and use analytics to see which posts drive subscriptions. The platform also streamlines notifications and supports cross-posting to other social channels, and AI agent integrations.

marketing.title: AI product recommendations are mostly a summary of listicles
marketing.summary: A study across 4 search engines found that 90% of recommended brands appeared on at least one cited “best X” or “top X” list. Brands featured on 3 or more cited lists were recommended 44% of the time, compared with just 2.5% for brands absent from all lists. The top 10 list publishers accounted for up to 90% of citations in some categories. Updated comparisons also mattered, with 83% of Gemini's cited pages featuring 2026 in the title or URL.

marketing.title: 3 things I'm watching in marketing going into 2027
marketing.summary: Brands are replacing some agency work with in-house creators and employee advocates to build trust through individual voices. Engaged communities are becoming more valuable than large follower counts as brands seek direct audience relationships beyond algorithm-dependent platforms. Meanwhile, audiences are tuning out generic claims of authenticity. Original perspectives and behind-the-scenes content are becoming more effective ways to stand out.

marketing.title: Why you WANT more unsubscribes
marketing.summary: A very low unsubscribe rate can mean email is landing in spam, since nobody unsubscribes from a junk folder. Unsubscribing is also the least damaging way to leave, since a spam report hurts placement and silent non-readers drag it down over time. Splitting unsubscribes by opt-in type separates intentional sign-ups, whose exits signal a content problem, from consequential ones like gated downloads, whose quick exits are expected. Making the exit easy, and occasionally inviting it, keeps people who are done from reaching for the spam button.

marketing.title: When Did ‘Grand Theft Auto' Become Brand Safe?
marketing.summary: GTA is no longer an automatic brand safety risk, but brands must weigh its cultural relevance against whether its provocative world fits their identity and audience.

marketing.title: Google Is Making More Room for News in AI Search
marketing.summary: Sites like Reddit report receiving less traffic from Google despite frequent appearances in AI answers.
